For testing, InjectMock can be used to inject a mock IMappedRegionRegistry.
In order to mock the MappedRegionFactory, we would need it to be a singleton (and
dispatch either to a mock or to the real implementation). In order to avoid having
a singleton but be able to mock the MappedRegionFactory, we would need to have the user
create and store an instance of the MappedRegionFactory themselves instead of the MemoryRegionRegistry.
This makes sense because the registry cannot exist without the factory. So rather than passing the
registry to factory calls, the registry would instead be owned by the factory instance.
The MappedRegionFactory owns the IMappedRegionRegistry since the registry makes no sense
without a factory (because without the factory, there are no resources and then the registry
The MappedRegionFactory is a friend of all MappedRegions and
can access their private constructors to create instances.
The GetId() method returns a unique identifier for the memory region
which depends on the specific memory type. E.g. a named region might
create the id by hashing the path name, an anonymous region might
use the anonymous handle id etc. It will be stored in the MemoryResourceProxy
and used to identify the memory region within the MemoryResourceRegistry.
